subject: application_plan
summary: W3 ApplicationPlan correctly applies standard OpenAPI + OCL for unauthorized reserve and unauthorized release (named UnauthorizedError; no hold; stock and existing holds unchanged), introduces a minimal release surface for the authZ deny path while deferring authorized restore to W4, defers formal with X8 / no concurrency_safety rationale, and explicitly preserves W1/W2 paths on shared SoT. Density is not thinned despite existing UnauthorizedError hooks on reserve. Lint minors (Brief 'sufficient', WorkPlan touches overlap) do not remove checkability.

findings.detail: lint: ambiguous phrase 'sufficient' in scope text
lint: overlapping touches on shared OpenAPI/OCL/src across W3–W5; serialize waves (W3 after W1/W2 already required)

W1 already exposes UnauthorizedError hooks on reserve in OpenAPI/OCL/impl/tests; plan correctly keeps status apply at standard rather than skip, but downstream apply-api/apply-dbc must elevate unauthorized no-mutation (including existing holds) and unauthorized release as first-class W3 checkable properties—not treat existing reserve hooks as done and no-op.

Slice scopes unauthorized failure on reserve + release only; authorized release restore (W4) and TTL expiry (W5) remain later items—acceptable isolation while R6/SC6 lifecycle completeness waits on those waves.
